answer: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed across hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (YBA, 1100–500 BCE), the principal component value of PC1 at the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE is markedly higher and represents the maximum peak (PC1 ≈ 4.45) of the entire sequence, whereas in the subsequent time horizons between 1000 and 500 BCE, the PC1 values drop sharply and display a persistent secular decline (dropping to 2.17 at 1000 BCE, 1.65 at 900 BCE, 1.91 at 800 BCE, 1.25 at 700 BCE, 0.83 at 600 BCE, and 0.82 at 500 BCE; mean subsequent PC1 = 1.44). This substantial reduction reflects a pronounced decrease in the key material capital forms driving PC1—specifically prestige metals such as copper and gold (ZCU_AU), daggers (ZDolch), monumental architecture count (ZMonument), house size (Zhausgr), and subsequent hoard depositions (ZHort).

payload.workflow: 1. Preprocesamiento y conversión de las 12 variables de capital en capital.csv a punto flotante. 2. Descomposición espectral/SVD de la matriz de covarianza y correlación sobre los 39 horizontes centenarios (4300–500 a. C.). 3. Orientación consistente del autovector PC1 según las cargas de riqueza material. 4. Proyección de las observaciones de la Younger Bronze Age (1100–500 a. C.) y cálculo de estadísticas comparativas.
payload.hypothesis: During the Younger Bronze Age (1100–500 BCE), PC1 at the beginning of the period (1100 BCE) reaches its peak value of approximately 4.45, whereas in the subsequent time horizons between 1000 and 500 BCE, PC1 exhibits a sharp and substantial decline to a range of 0.82–2.17 (mean = 1.44), driven by the steep reduction in prestige metalwork (copper/gold and daggers), domestic house size, and monument density.
